title: Evented span batcher, OTEL upgrade and async log-writer refactor
creator: Amaya Singh
description: Background: Our current observability pipeline relies on synchronous span flush paths and a legacy OpenTelemetry client pinned at 1.12. Several high-throughput services report elevated p95 tail latency and CPU spikes when trace throughput increases. Logs and metric emitters share a small set of sync writers which produce backpressure into request threads. Problem: request latency and CPU/cold-path allocations increase under load; memory churn from span objects and synchronous log writers contributes to GC pressure. Goal: upgrade OTEL client to a supported LTS version, replace sync writers with an evented async span batcher, and refactor our log writer to a bounded, non-blocking background queue with backpressure controls. This ticket covers the core runtime changes, integration tests, rollout plan, and initial dashboards to verify SLA behavior.
acceptance_criteria: OTEL client upgraded to 1.16 with no semantic-compat regressions in span attributes
New evented span batcher reduces per-request median allocation by >= 20% in warm path
Sync log writers removed from request hot path; background writer handles bursts with bounded queue
No increase in dropped spans above baseline (<= 0.5% increase during high load testing)
Observability dashboards show p50/p95 request latency unchanged or improved after rollout
technical_decision: We will adopt an event-driven span batching model: instrumented requests enqueue lightweight span handles into a lock-free MPSC queue. A small pool of background workers will coalesce spans into batches and export via OTEL gRPC exporter. To limit memory growth, spans will retain only the necessary KV pairs until flush; full serialization is deferred to worker threads. For logs, we'll replace the sync file/console writer with an async ring-buffer + background flusher with droppable policy for non-critical debug level to avoid unbounded backlog. Chose OTEL 1.16 because it contains required propagation fixes and exporter stability patches; the migration will use a compatibility shim for our custom span attributes to avoid application-level changes immediately. Trade-offs: small increase in background thread count and memory for queues versus significant latency and allocation reductions on request threads. This matches our production-first performance goals.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature branch behind feature flag; 2) Run integration load tests in staging (synthetic traces, spikes, flamegraph comparisons); 3) Canary rollout to 5% of traffic for 24h; monitor trace/dropped-span rate, request P95, CPU and GC; 4) Expand to 25% for 24h; 5) Full rollout. Emergency rollback: toggle feature flag to disable evented batcher and revert exporter config to legacy synchronous flush path. Contingency: if exporter errors spike, route traces to fallback exporter (local buffer + later retry).
